title: Synthetic Paragraph Argument Holdout — 200 Original Cases (v1)
origin: Original AI-authored fictional examples; labels written before any model predictions; not sourced from real people, news or user accounts.
annotation: Author-provided reference labels with short rationales. Not independently human-adjudicated. Review any disputed labels separately; do not silently alter this frozen v1 corpus.
intended_split: 200 new cases: 50 supported, 50 unsupported, 50 contradictory, 25 explicit-but-undetermined, 25 without an inference.
evaluation_protocol: Run once on the frozen main-branch analyser after merge, record results and source commit. Do not tune to this corpus; use a separate development dataset and test against a v2 blind holdout later.

cases.text: Town regulations require every hot-food stall at the quay to hold a hygiene permit. The cedar kiosk sells hot meals at the quay, so it is subject to the hygiene-permit requirement.
cases.label_rationale: The universal permit rule applies to an explicitly described member of its class.

cases.text: The competition tally contains 26 votes for Elm and 19 for Ash. Therefore Elm received seven more votes than Ash.
cases.label_rationale: The conclusion is the exact arithmetic difference between two stated totals.

cases.text: Every parcel weighing more than 15 kilograms must travel on the freight lift. This parcel weighs 18 kilograms, so the freight-lift rule applies to it.

cases.text: The exhibition ends on 30 April, and tonight is 1 May. Consequently the exhibition has already ended.

cases.text: If the reservoir level drops below four metres, the intake pump shuts down. The gauge now reads 3.6 metres, so the stated shutdown condition has been met.

cases.text: The regional tournament admits only clubs registered before January. The Falcons registered in November of the previous year and have been admitted, so their registration preceded January.

cases.text: All seven envelopes in the drawer were sealed this morning. The red envelope is one of those seven, so the red envelope was sealed this morning.

cases.text: The taxi fare is £12 plus £3 for each of two extra stops. Therefore this journey costs £18 before any tip.

cases.label_rationale: The conclusion is conditional and tentative, not a definite attendance outcome.

cases.text: The new timetable leaves a longer gap between two late buses. This suggests the evening journey could feel less convenient to some passengers.
cases.label_rationale: A qualified perception forecast is not a demonstrated outcome or explicit contradiction.

cases.text: The council has asked residents to comment on a draft zoning plan. Consequently some of the proposed boundaries may change after consultation.
cases.label_rationale: Consultation creates a possibility, not an asserted final change.

cases.text: The workshop has trialled a quieter ventilation setting. Thus participants might find the room more comfortable next week.
cases.label_rationale: The future comfort claim is hedged and the effect has not been observed.

cases.text: The retailer will test a different shelf arrangement in one branch. Therefore the change might help shoppers locate products more quickly.
cases.label_rationale: A trial of layout offers only a tentative future benefit.

cases.text: The rehearsal was moved from the afternoon to the morning. As a result, some performers could find the new schedule easier to manage.
cases.label_rationale: The conclusion describes a possible response by unspecified people.

cases.text: The museum is considering bilingual signs at its entrance. This means visitors may eventually see information in another language.
cases.label_rationale: The asserted possibility depends on a decision not yet made.

cases.text: The neighbourhood group has arranged a public meeting about traffic. Hence the discussion could identify an option that has not previously been considered.
cases.label_rationale: Possible discovery in a future discussion is not directly established or refuted.

cases.text: A garden nursery has offered to sponsor seed packets at the school. Therefore the pupils might be able to plant more varieties in spring.
cases.label_rationale: Sponsorship and planting are contingent, not a definite causal conclusion.

cases.text: The committee delayed its vote to obtain another engineering report. Consequently the final decision may differ from the current proposal.
cases.label_rationale: The statement is an explicitly uncertain future decision.

cases.text: The theatre is experimenting with shorter intervals. This suggests audience feedback could be different at the next performance.
cases.label_rationale: A possible feedback change is not a certain fact established by the experiment.

cases.text: A construction team expects to use a quieter concrete mixer. Therefore nearby residents might notice less noise during the next pour.
cases.label_rationale: The equipment is prospective and the effect is qualified.

cases.text: The printer has been serviced after intermittent paper jams. Hence it may run more smoothly when the next large document is printed.
cases.label_rationale: Maintenance may help but does not establish the next print outcome.

cases.text: The university has added an optional evening tutorial. So students with jobs could find it easier to attend a class.
cases.label_rationale: The outcome is a possibility conditional on individual schedules.

cases.text: The campsite is taking reservations for an extra autumn weekend. Consequently some guests might choose to extend their holidays.
cases.label_rationale: Availability does not establish a specific guest's future choice.

cases.text: The council is reviewing the location of a pedestrian crossing. Therefore the eventual design could put the crossing a little farther uphill.
cases.label_rationale: The proposed location remains unsettled.

cases.text: The local newspaper has recruited a science correspondent. This means its science coverage might become more detailed.
cases.label_rationale: A tentative editorial quality outcome is not established solely by a hire.

cases.text: The delivery firm is assessing electric cargo bikes for short routes. Consequently some routes may eventually require fewer van journeys.
cases.label_rationale: An assessment does not certify future implementation, and the conclusion is tentative.

cases.text: The town has created a small grant programme for musicians. Thus some applicants might be able to hold events they previously could not afford.
cases.label_rationale: The conclusion depends on selection, costs and future actions, and is hedged.

cases.text: A restaurant is trying a different dough recipe in its kitchen. Therefore the new version might appeal to customers who disliked the old one.
cases.label_rationale: Preference changes are hypothetical rather than a stated observed fact.

cases.text: The technology team intends to simplify its sign-in screen. This suggests fewer users could become confused by the next version.
cases.label_rationale: The interface is not yet deployed and the claimed effect is qualified.

cases.text: The recreation centre has proposed a morning yoga class. Hence more residents may consider visiting the centre before work.
cases.label_rationale: A proposed class and future interest are possibilities, not known outcomes.

cases.text: The publishing house has asked several illustrators for sketches. As a result, the book's eventual cover might look different from the initial mock-up.
cases.label_rationale: The future design is expressly uncertain.

cases.text: The transit authority is exploring ways to shorten ticket queues. Therefore the average waiting time could fall if a suitable system is adopted.
cases.label_rationale: The claimed improvement is conditional on adoption and effectiveness.

cases.text: The orchard manager plans to inspect the trees before harvest. Consequently the inspection might reveal problems that were not visible earlier.
cases.label_rationale: The result of a future inspection is not known and is described only as possible.

cases.text: The exhibition catalogue was printed in two editions, one in English and one in Welsh. Both editions contain the same photographs.
cases.label_rationale: Two descriptive facts are presented without a proposed inference.

cases.text: In 2024 the café closed at 17:00, but this year it closes at 18:00. The change is noted on the entrance notice.
cases.label_rationale: Different dates describe a change, not contradictory simultaneous assertions or a conclusion.

cases.text: The chair described how the committee arrived at its decision. The explanation was recorded in the published minutes.
cases.label_rationale: Reporting that an explanation exists is not asserting an inference in this passage.

cases.text: A red line marks the pedestrian area on the site plan. The map key also identifies bicycle parking beside the western gate.
cases.label_rationale: The paragraph supplies map facts without an inferential claim.

cases.text: The artist said, “We sold out, so everyone loves us.” The interviewer did not endorse that statement.
cases.label_rationale: An attributed quotation is reported rather than advanced as the narrator's argument.

cases.text: The organisers arranged extra microphones so that people in the rear rows could hear the panel. Sound engineers checked the equipment before the doors opened.
cases.label_rationale: The words so that express purpose rather than an argument conclusion.

cases.text: Because of heavy fog, the harbour office postponed the crossing. The revised departure time was posted later.
cases.label_rationale: A causal event report introduced by because of is not a tested argument in this schema.

cases.text: The exhibition has been travelling since 2021. Its latest stop is a municipal gallery near the river.
cases.label_rationale: Since marks a date, not an inferential connector.

cases.text: The website's home page includes a calendar, a directory and a contact form. Its accessibility statement is in the footer.
cases.label_rationale: These are inventory observations with no explicit conclusion.

cases.text: A reporter asked whether the scheme had met its targets. The director said the figures were being audited.
cases.label_rationale: A question and attributed reply are not the reporter's own inferred conclusion.

cases.text: The first train leaves the valley at dawn. The last return trip is scheduled for 21:30.
cases.label_rationale: Two schedule facts are stated without drawing an inference.

cases.text: The team wanted to improve the readability of the leaflet. It changed the heading sizes and increased the margins.
cases.label_rationale: Actions and motivations are described without claiming a logical conclusion.

cases.text: The term “green corridor” is used in the planning document to describe a route between parks. The council has published a map of that route.
cases.label_rationale: A term's definition and a publication fact do not form an explicit argument.

cases.text: Three friends travelled to the festival together. They purchased separate return tickets and shared a picnic.
cases.label_rationale: A narrative sequence without a proposed inferential claim.

cases.text: The company announced a new annual report last Tuesday. The report is scheduled for publication next month.
cases.label_rationale: A publication timeline is described without an asserted conclusion.

cases.text: Please check the size chart before ordering a uniform. The return instructions are printed at the back of the booklet.
cases.label_rationale: An instruction and a descriptive detail do not constitute an inferential argument.

cases.text: The survey includes questions about commuting, food shopping and public spaces. Respondents can skip any question they prefer.
cases.label_rationale: Survey design facts are given without any explicit deduction.

cases.text: The conservation group monitors butterfly habitats each spring. Its volunteers also record rainfall for the local archive.
cases.label_rationale: Two activities are reported, neither offered as evidence for a conclusion.

cases.text: The board discussed the budget on Monday and the staffing plan on Wednesday. The meeting notes distinguish the two topics.
cases.label_rationale: Events on separate days are not presented as inferentially linked claims.

cases.text: The cooking demonstration covered bread making, food storage and knife care. Participants received a copy of the recipe booklet.
cases.label_rationale: Event details are presented without a conclusion.

cases.text: Some readers praised the article while others questioned its sources. The editor printed several letters from both groups.
cases.label_rationale: Differing views are attributed, not endorsed as the text's own inference.

cases.text: The ferry captain spoke about the route during a radio interview. The port authority later published the updated schedule.
cases.label_rationale: Sequential news items are not an explicit inference.

cases.text: The trial's methods section explains that participants completed a short questionnaire. The answers were stored without names.
cases.label_rationale: A study procedure and data-handling fact form a description, not a conclusion.

cases.text: The council notice lists the dates for repairing the pavement. Residents can contact the works office with access questions.
cases.label_rationale: Information and contact instructions are not an inferred assertion.

cases.text: The museum shop sells postcards, pencils and reproductions of historical maps. A second counter opens during busy afternoons.
cases.label_rationale: The paragraph inventories services without asserting a causal or deductive conclusion.
